respondent:
Municipal Committee
Supreme Court of India

21 February 1957
Writ Petition (civil) 660 of 1954
The Judgment was delivered by : Hon'ble Justice Syed Jafer Imam
1. This is an application u/art. 32 of the Constitution against the Municipal Committee of Bhatapara (hereinafter referred to as "the Municipality") alleging that the petitioner's fundamental rights guaranteed by Art. 19(1)(j) and Art. 14 of the Constitution have been violated by the Action of the Municipality.
2. In Bhatapara there is a market vested in the Municipality known as "Ganj" the use of which is regulated by its bye-laws framed u/s. 179 of the Central Provinces and Berar Municipalities Act (Act 2 of 1922) (hereinafter referred to as the Act). At this market transactions of sale and purchase of grain take place. According to the petitioner, he is an Adatya by occupation and carries on his trade as such for sellers of grain in the said market. He has been prevented from carrying on his trade as an Adatya
facts: In Bhatapara there is a market vested in the Municipality known as 'Ganj' the use of which is regulated by its bye-laws framed u/s.
According to the petitioner, he is an Adatya by occupation and carries on his trade as such for sellers of grain in the said market.
He has been prevented from carrying on his trade as an Adatya of sellers of grain in the said market by the Municipality in pursuance of a resolution passed by it on 4-9-1949.
The employees of the Municipality have been directed under the resolution to stop issuing Ganj receipts to the petitioner.
There has thus been discrimination on the part of the Municipality.
In 1935, the Government of the Central Provinces published a notification confirming the bye-laws framed by the Municipality.
These bye-laws contained provisions for regulating the use of the market at Bhatapara.

The bye-law proposed by this resolution stated: 'The Municipal Committee shall appoint licensed Adhatias (commission agents) in the Ganj who will help the sellers in prompt disposal of their grains and shall make payment to them of their grains immediately after its measurement.'
The State Government did not confirm the bye-law but required the Municipality to submit a Statement of Objects and Reasons for the proposed amendment of its bye-laws.

Thereafter, the Municipality considered the communication of the Government and passed the following resolution on 4-9-1949: 'Now the Committee does not desire to adopt the system of Arhatiyas in its Ganj. The subject is therefore dropped.'

U/s. 53 of the Act, the Deputy Commissioner is authorised, in certain circumstances, to suspend a resolution passed by a Municipality and he was accordingly approached to exercise his power under that section to suspend the abovementioned resolution.

The Additional Deputy Commissioner made a report on which the Deputy Commissioner suspended for a month the resolution passed by the Municipality on 4-9-1949, calling upon the Municipality to submit an explanation.
After considering the explanation and hearing the parties concerned, he declined to set aside the resolution passed by the Municipality.
The order of the Deputy Commissioner was passed on 7-11-1951.

The petitioner filed an application u/art. 226 of the Constitution in the High Court of Judicature at Nagpur which was duly considered by the learned Judges of that Court which was dismissed on 18-1-1954.
The petitioner did not file a petition for special leave in this Court, but filed the present application u/art. 32 of the Constitution on 10-12-1954.
issues: Whether any fundamental right of the petitioner has been violated or that he has been discriminated against by the Municipality.
Whether the bye-laws framed by the Municipality violate any fundamental right of any citizen of India.
petitioner_arguments: The petitioner relied upon two Nakka receipts, Annexures B-1 and B-2 to his petition, in support of his allegation that while he is not permitted to transact business as an Adatya of sellers of grain other Adatyas are permitted to do so.

The bye-law proposed by this resolution stated: 'The Municipal Committee shall appoint licensed Adhatias (commission agents) in the Ganj who will help the sellers in prompt disposal of their grains and shall make payment to them of their grains immediately after its measurement.'
respondent_arguments: According to the case of the Municipality, all Adatyas of sellers of grain are refused Ganj receipts in their names as it was discovered that the owners of the grain who brought their produce to the market for sale were being victimised.
The bye-laws of the Municipality contain no provision for the issuing of Nakka and Ganj receipts and passes in the name of the Adatya of the owner of the grain brought for sale.
court_reasoning: We are, accordingly of the opinion that there is no reliable material before us to establish that the petitioner is being discriminated against.
What we have to decide is whether a person who is not the owner of the grain to be sold in the market has a similar right.
The bye-laws of the Municipality contain no provision for the issuing of Nakka and Ganj receipts and passes in the name of the Adatya of the owner of the grain brought for sale.
holding: We are of the opinion that there is no reliable material before us to establish that the petitioner is being discriminated against.
The bye-laws framed by the Municipality do not violate any fundamental right of any citizen of India.
The resolution dated 4-9-1949 did not violate any fundamental right of the petitioner.
